title: Persistence of a specified cocartesian edge in a filtered colimit
statement:
Use the universes and coherent quasicategories of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], small filtered infinity categories of [def-coef-presentable-infinity-category], and $\operatorname{Cat}_\infty$, intrinsic cocartesian edges and infinity-categorical slices of [lem-coef-cocartesian-straightening]. Let $B$ be a small infinity category and $D:I\to\operatorname{Cat}_{\infty/B}$ a small filtered coherent diagram, with structural functors $p_j:E_j\to B$. Let $p:E\to B$ with legs $r_j:E_j\to E$ be a colimiting cocone in that slice whose underlying cocone is colimiting in $\operatorname{Cat}_\infty$. Fix $i\in I$ and an edge $e:x\to y$ in $E_i$. Suppose that, for every $u:i\to j$ in the coherent coslice $I_{i/}$, the edge $D(u)e$ is $p_j$-cocartesian. Then $r_i(e)$ is $p$-cocartesian. In particular, for every $z\in E$ and $g:p(r_i y)\to p(z)$, precomposition with $r_i(e)$ induces an equivalence
$$\operatorname{Map}^{g}_{E}(r_i y,z)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Map}^{g\,p(r_i e)}_{E}(r_i x,z).$$
Here $\operatorname{Map}^{h}$ means the homotopy fiber of the map on mapping spaces over the specified base arrow $h$, with the slice coherences identifying the bases. No cocartesian lifts other than the indicated transition images are assumed, and no transition functor is assumed fully faithful.

source.place: Proposition 3.3.2, proof of (ii): the mapping square for the image of a specified stage lift, allowing only its transition images as later lifts; read online, not archived in literature/. No Stacks tag states this infinity-categorical assertion.

proof.text: Fix $z\in E$ and write $b=p(z)$. Apply the fixed-base-change clause of [lem-coef-cat-infinity-filtered-finite-calculus] with $T=\{b\}\to B$: the infinity-categorical fiber $E_b$ is the filtered colimit of $(E_j)_b$. Apply its object-representation clause to this fiber diagram to choose $z_j\in(E_j)_b$ and an equivalence $r_jz_j\simeq z$ in $E_b$. Filteredness, in the finite-cocone sense of [def-coef-presentable-infinity-category], gives a stage $k$ and arrows $u:i\to k$, $v:j\to k$. Set $x_k=D(u)x$, $y_k=D(u)y$, $e_k=D(u)e$, and $z_k=D(v)z_j$. The slice coherences and the fiber equivalence identify their bases with $p(r_i x)$, $p(r_i y)$ and $b$. Thus any specified arrow $g:p(r_i y)\to b$ is a fixed base arrow for these objects and their further transition images. The coherent coslice $J=I_{k/}$ is small and filtered by the same finite-calculus statement.

source.place: Proposition 3.3.2, proof of (ii), using the filtered-colimit mapping-space and common-stage calculation

proof.text:
For $w:k\to l$ in $J$, put $e_w=D(w)e_k$ and $z_w=D(w)z_k$. The coherent composition of $w$ with $u$ identifies $e_w$ with a transition image $D(wu)e$, so it is $p_l$-cocartesian by hypothesis. The intrinsic mapping-square criterion of [lem-coef-cocartesian-straightening], pulled back over the point $g$ of $\operatorname{Map}_B(p(r_i y),b)$, gives an equivalence
$$A_w:=\operatorname{Map}^{g}_{E_l}(D(w)y_k,z_w)\longrightarrow C_w:=\operatorname{Map}^{g\,p(e_w)}_{E_l}(D(w)x_k,z_w).$$
Indeed the pullback square says that the comparison from its upper left corner to the homotopy pullback $P_w$ of the upper right corner along base precomposition is an equivalence. The only-if direction of [lem-coef-spaces-homotopy-fiber-detection], with bottom map the identity of $\operatorname{Map}_B(p(r_i y),b)$, gives an equivalence of homotopy fibers over $g$; the homotopy fiber of $P_w$ over $g$ is that of the right vertical map over $g\,p(e_w)$, since both are limits of the same cospan. This gives exactly these two homotopy fibers. These maps form a coherent transformation $A\to C$ on $J$: [lem-coef-infinity-hom-bifunctor-functoriality] states coherent naturality of mapping-space maps and preservation of composition under every transition functor. The slice coherences identify the base maps and their homotopy fibers throughout this transformation. This uses only the images of $e$.

source.place: Proposition 3.3.2, proof of (ii), mapping square for the image of a specified stage lift

proof.text: The pointwise-equivalence criterion of [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus] makes $A\to C$ an equivalence of $J$-diagrams of spaces. Its inverse transformation and the two inverse homotopies induce inverse maps between the colimits, so $\operatorname{colim}_J A\to\operatorname{colim}_J C$ is an equivalence. These small space colimits exist by [lem-coef-spaces-small-colimits-universe]. Apply the relative mapping-space comparison of [lem-coef-cat-infinity-filtered-finite-calculus] to the two pairs $(y_k,z_k)$ and $(x_k,z_k)$ in the original diagram indexed by $I$. It identifies these two colimits with $\operatorname{Map}^{g}_E(r_k y_k,r_k z_k)$ and $\operatorname{Map}^{g\,p(r_ke_k)}_E(r_k x_k,r_k z_k)$. Its stated naturality in precomposition and under maps to $B$ identifies the induced colimit map with precomposition by $r_ke_k$. The cocone identifies this edge with $r_i e$. Postcomposition with the fiber equivalence $r_kz_k\simeq z$ gives inverse equivalences of the two relative mapping spaces, with inverse given by its inverse edge; their inverse homotopies remain over the base identity. We obtain the asserted relative precomposition equivalence for the original $z$ and $g$.

source.place: Proposition 3.3.2, proof of (ii), passage from stage mapping squares to the colimit

proof.text: For fixed $z$, abbreviate $Y=\operatorname{Map}_E(r_i y,z)$, $X=\operatorname{Map}_E(r_i x,z)$, $S=\operatorname{Map}_B(p(r_i y),p(z))$ and $T=\operatorname{Map}_B(p(r_i x),p(z))$. Let $P=X\times^h_T S$. Precomposition and its functoriality give a comparison $Y\to P$ over $S$. For every vertex $g\in S$, its homotopy-fiber map identifies with the map proved to be an equivalence in step 3: the fiber of $P\to S$ at $g$ is the homotopy fiber of $X\to T$ at $g\,p(r_i e)$. This identification follows by the pullback universal property, since both sides are the limit of $X\to T\leftarrow\{g\,p(r_i e)\}$. Apply [lem-coef-spaces-homotopy-fiber-detection] with bottom map $1_S$. It makes $Y\to P$ an equivalence, including when $S$ or its fibers are empty. Hence the intrinsic mapping square is a homotopy pullback for every $z$. The characterization in [lem-coef-cocartesian-straightening] proves that $r_i(e)$ is $p$-cocartesian.

proof_origin.place: Proposition 3.3.2(ii), especially the proof of the mapping square for a specified stage lift; source read online 2026-10-17 and not archived in literature.
